key_insight: Ethylenediamine reconstructs tin-rich tin–lead perovskite surfaces toward a stoichiometric tin-to-lead ratio, improving electron extraction and suppressing interfacial nonradiative recombination.
engineering_relevance: Controlling molecular protonation and surface defects offers a route to more efficient methylammonium-free perovskite solar cells.
method: Use neutral ethylenediamine to chelate undercoordinated metals and remove excess surface tin.
Compare this reconstruction with ethylenediammonium iodide passivation and defect-assisted deprotonation.
Use atomistic simulations to probe vacancy-assisted iodide migration and deprotonation energetics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25.86% power conversion efficiency and simulations showing that subsurface iodide vacancies lower the energetic cost of deprotonation.
watch_item: The abstract does not report long-term operational stability or scalability of the surface treatment.
paper_title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
